title: epan: fix Coverity Resource leak
description:
Use `wmem_strbuf_finalize()` and `char*` to fix the resource leak.

Coverity CID 1680294

```
12. alloc_fn: Storage is returned from allocation function wmem_strbuf_new.
13. var_assign: Assigning: tac_name = storage returned from wmem_strbuf_new(addr_resolv_scope, cp).

CID 1680294: (#2 of 2): Resource leak (RESOURCE_LEAK)
22. overwrite_var: Overwriting tac_name in tac_name = wmem_strbuf_new(addr_resolv_scope, cp) leaks the storage that tac_name points to.
    tac_name = wmem_strbuf_new(addr_resolv_scope, cp);

14. noescape: Resource tac_name is not freed or pointed-to in wmem_strbuf_get_str.
    mem_map_insert(tac_hash_table, GUINT_TO_POINTER(id), (void *)wmem_strbuf_get_str(tac_name));
```

If all this is doing is duplicating the string, I'm not sure there's a point in the wmem_strbuf_t.

Just passing `(void *)wmem_strdup(addr_resolv_scope, cp)` as the final parameter to the `wmem_map_insert` seems fine.

So we are in a `while()` loop.

If id is not found in the hash table it creates a new wmem_strbuf_t and adds the wmem_strbuf_get_str() (char*) output to the hash table.

Instead, I would use wmem_strbuf_finalize() which covers the resource leak and also adds (char*) output to the hash table.

With this we do not let the memory grow with every loop which creates a new wmem_strbuf and also eliminate (hopefully) the Coverity resource leak.
yes, I see your point but I cannot fully test it.
do you want me to update the MR with your suggestion?
but I think that would also raise a coverity resource leak issue so it would not be much better than we have now....

Yes, that would work.

I think it would not raise a Coverity resource leak because the string is being placed inside the hash table; at least, if Coverity still complains then it would complain about using `wmem_strbuf_finalize` too (which also allocates a string as it frees the growable string). That is why Coverity does not have resource leak complaints about the other functions in addr_resolv.c

The problem with the existing code is that while the string inside the wmem_strbuf_t is placed in the hash table, that's only part of the struct.
